bit_exact_detail: Every output hash (GEMM outputs, projection logits, greedy (max, index) pairs, certified-screen pairs, split-K outputs) is equal across all four ABBA runs of both arms in every cell, across both TILE_CONFIGS[128] variants and both screen-config sets, and in the A/A rerun; every diagnosis variant (gemm base/pdl/rb/963, vocab base/963/exc/dec) gives the same bits: 0 ULP.
slot_effect_note: In one process, two layers with identical kernels can differ by up to 7% in graph replay (h963r1 section D: the second-built layer 3-5% faster at TP4 M<=64 on both arms; d963 sab: monotone with the build order at TP3 M=1). Every #963-r1 comparison here is therefore cross-arm at the same layer slot (same set, same config), and the in-process diagnosis of the screen decode is left inconclusive.
reason: The corrected 0782 keeps #963's gains where they hold and is the base's machine code wherever #963 lost on a path serving uses. Gains, by CUDA-graph replay, beyond the interval, 0 ULP: packed BF16 GEMM 5120x512 (compressor_up, the mark) faster at all 8 M (1.023-1.094x, e.g. M=1 7.27/7.27 -> 6.65/6.64 us) and 4096x1280 at all 8 (1.015-1.086x); packed vocab projection faster in all 26 cells (2.44-3.82x at the PR's 0.35% exception density; at the same TILE_CONFIGS[128] on both arms 20/20), greedy partials in all 22 (2.40-3.80x; same config 12/12). Restored: the certified screen's kernels (vllm_vocab_decode_vec16 is the base's: byte-identical SASS for every screen, refine, threshold, x-norm, compact and finish kernel in both arms), serving's split-K compressor GEMM and the prefill unpack (vllm_packed_bf16_filter_exc is the base's: identical SASS), and packed_bf16_gemm on the narrow 512x10240 and 128x5120 grids (the base's search and launch: identical SASS), which read same at all 16 M (0.986-1.005x) where the first version was 2-7.4% slower. The own mark's screen miss (TP4 M=97..120 0.974-0.994x) is gone: at the same screen set the screen reads same or faster at 97, 107, 112, 120, 128 and 0.994x at 104. The few slower readings on identical SASS (screen s4a2 set TP4 M=6, 17, 24, 104 by 0.2-0.6%; r1 set TP3 M=120 0.950x) are the interval rule's noise: an A/A rerun of the screen and split-K sections (ABBA, 2 boots per arm, same SASS) gives 16 such slower readings in 76 cells (0.2-4.4%), TP4 s4a2 M=6, 17 and 24 among them again (0.4-0.5%: the arms' placement, not their code), while TP3 r1 M=120 reads 1.045x faster there and TP4 r1 M=120 0.956x slower. The PR's own diagnosis that the decode rewrite cuts unpack ALU did not show as time: within 0.5% in the projection and greedy partials at both densities, so it is dropped.
